chunks: Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isam al-Kulayni (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kulayni narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Muhammad, known as 'Allan al-Kulayni, narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Isa ibn Ubayd narrated to us, saying: I asked Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad al-Askari (peace be upon them both)

about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: 'The earth, all of it, is His grasp on the Day of Resurrection, and the Heavens are bent in His Right.' He said: That is the expression of Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, to he who likened Him to His creation. Do you not see that He said: 'And they did not appraise Allah His true appraisal' when they said: 'The earth, all of it, is His grasp on the Day of Resurrection, and the Heavens are bent in His Right'? As He, Exalted and Glorious is He, said: 'And they did not appraise Allah His true appraisal, when they said: Allah did not send down unto a human being, anything.' Then, He, Exalted and Glorious is He, exalted Himself from the grasp and the right hand, so He said: 'Glorified is He, and Exalted, from what they associate.'
ai.seo_question: How does the Imam explain the concept of Allah's 'grasp' and 'right hand' in relation to anthropomorphism?
ai.summary: Imam al-Askari (peace be upon him) elucidates that the Quranic descriptions of Allah's 'grasp' and 'right hand' serve as a rebuke (ta'ir) to those who anthropomorphize the Divine by likening Him to His creation. By linking these verses to 'And they did not appraise Allah His true appraisal,' he clarifies that these physical metaphors highlight human limitation in comprehending God's essence, leading to the exaltation of Allah from physical attributes like a literal hand or grasp.
